methodology: Expanding, selected, attributed incident and regional report catalogue affecting Assyrian people and historically linked Syriac and other Christian church communities. Entries may cover distinct single events, town-level episodes, or broad campaigns, with overlapping episodes sometimes cross-referenced in their descriptions. Source evidence ranges from scholarly history and formal human-rights reports to attributed community accounts. A reported allegation is not presented as a proven finding. The heat map represents the number of catalogue entries, not victims, severity, persecution rates, or unique campaigns. Country inclusion follows the recorded location of an event, not the residence of witnesses or exiles. Place coordinates are approximate and may identify only the town or region. Unrepresented countries do not imply absence of persecution. Soviet-era reports are mapped to the present-day geographic country where the action occurred, without attributing responsibility to current independent governments or the modern ethnic populations of those states.

records.title: Assyrian Mor Yukhana church and Qujsnaya village damaged during daesh occupation
records.summary: SyriacPress reported in September 2021 from Qujsnaya (also called Tel Demchej) that the village had been largely destroyed during daesh attacks on Assyrian Khabur settlements in 2015. The Church of Mor Yukhana (St John) showed damaged furnishings, graffiti and signs of vandalism, while many former residents remained displaced. Its condition was observed in 2021, which is not the same as a precisely dated independent 2021 attack. This is a locality-level case within the regional Khabur campaign already represented in AP-0020 and AP-0062.
